newsitem.title: USA: Shieldmate denies charges in Motorola suit.
newsitem.headline: Shieldmate denies charges in Motorola suit.

text.p: Shieldmate Robotics Inc said it denied and "strenuously disputed" allegations made against it by Motorola Inc in a recently filed lawsuit.
Motorola sued Shieldmate and Qualcomm Inc, a cellular telephone maker that is among Shieldmate's customers, charging patent infringement with regard to its cellular telephones.
"At no time in the history of this company have we passed along the design secrets of one client to another," Shieldmate President Steve Matecki said in a statement.
Shieldmate said it makes plastic housings for Motorola's StarTAC phone and for the Qualcomm "Q" phone.
"We simply manufacture the housings based on the designs of our clients, in this case Motorola and Qualcomm," Matecki said. "We don't actually design them."

He said both the Q phone and Motorola's StarTAC phone are based on a "clam shell" design, which he said is common to laptop computers, calculators and other devices. He added that the two phones use different technologies and other different functions.
